title: When your “mind’s eye” is blank: Understanding aphantasia, with Joel Pearson, PhD

sentences.en: Try to picture an apple.
sentences.zh: 试着想象一个苹果。

sentences.en: For most people, that's easy.
sentences.zh: 对大多数人来说，这很简单。

sentences.en: The word conjures up an image in their mind's eye of a round red fruit with a brown stem, maybe a green leaf on the top.
sentences.zh: 这个词会在他们的脑海中勾勒出一个圆圆的、红色的水果，带着棕色的梗，顶部可能还有一片绿叶。

sentences.en: But for people with aphantasia, it's impossible.
sentences.zh: 但对于患有心盲症的人来说，这是不可能的。

sentences.en: Trying to picture an apple or anything else brings up nothing but essentially a blank screen.
sentences.zh: 试图想象苹果或其他任何东西，只会浮现出一片空白，本质上就像一个空白屏幕。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk with one of the world's leading experts on aphantasia or the inability to visualize things in one's mind's eye about what scientists are
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与一位世界领先的心盲症（即无法在脑海中进行视觉化想象）专家探讨科学家们

sentences.en: learning about this recently identified condition.
sentences.zh: 对这一近期才被识别出的病症有哪些了解。

sentences.en: What causes aphantasia?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致了心盲症？

sentences.en: How common is it?
sentences.zh: 它有多普遍？

sentences.en: How do you reliably measure a person's inner experience, like the ability to form mental images?
sentences.zh: 你如何可靠地测量一个人的内心体验，比如形成心理意象的能力？

sentences.en: What effects might aphantasia have on people's lives, from memory to creativity to mental health?
sentences.zh: 心盲症会对人们的生活产生什么影响，从记忆力到创造力，再到心理健康？

sentences.en: And what can studying aphantasia tell us more broadly about how the human mind works?
sentences.zh: 研究心盲症能让我们更广泛地了解人类思维是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Joel Pearson, a professor in the School of Psychology and director of the Future
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是乔尔·皮尔逊博士，他是澳大利亚新南威尔士大学心理学院教授兼未来

sentences.en: Minds Lab at the University of New South Wales in Australia.
sentences.zh: 思维实验室主任。

sentences.en: He is a cognitive neuroscientist whose research explores intuition, the human imagination, aphantasia, and the psychological impact of artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 他是一位认知神经科学家，其研究探索了直觉、人类想象力、心盲症以及人工智能对心理的影响。

sentences.en: He's a sought-after speaker, author, and writer who has published dozens of peer-reviewed research articles and whose work has been covered by media outlets, including
sentences.zh: 他是一位广受欢迎的演讲者、作家和撰稿人，发表过数十篇同行评审的研究论文，其工作被包括

sentences.en: The New Yorker, ABC Australia, and The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约客》、《澳大利亚广播公司》和《纽约时报》在内的媒体报道过。

sentences.en: Dr. Pearson, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 皮尔逊博士，感谢您今天参加节目。

sentences.en: My pleasure, Kim.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸，金。

sentences.en: Great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: I described aphantasia in the introduction a moment ago, but let's start with a little more context in history for our listeners.
sentences.zh: 刚才在介绍中我已经描述了心盲症，但让我们先为听众提供更多的背景和历史信息。

sentences.en: So can you tell us more about what exactly aphantasia is and how long have scientists recognized it as a distinct condition?
sentences.zh: 那么，您能详细告诉我们心盲症究竟是什么，以及科学家们将其认定为一种独特的病症有多久了？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's generally considered the inability to visualize.
sentences.zh: 它通常被认为是无法进行视觉化想象。

sentences.en: So sometimes people will use the phrase imagination, but that's a very broad phrase that people get confused with creativity and other things.
sentences.zh: 有时人们会使用“想象力”这个词，但这是一个非常宽泛的词，人们常把它与创造力及其他事物混淆。

sentences.en: So it's really the inability to visualize typically visual mental imagery.
sentences.zh: 所以它实际上是指无法进行典型的视觉心理意象构建。

sentences.en: And we'll unpack some of the other senses a little bit later.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会进一步拆解其他感官方面的内容。

sentences.en: So mainly it's talked about or referred to as the inability to visualize.
sentences.zh: 所以它主要被称为或被定义为无法进行视觉化想象。

sentences.en: So when you think about, like you said in the introduction, what an apple might look like
sentences.zh: 正如您在介绍中所说，当你思考一个苹果看起来是什么样时，

sentences.en: for someone like me who has mental imagery, I have this sort of momentary glimpse of a conscious experience of the colors and shapes of the apple.
sentences.zh: 对于像我这样有心理意象的人来说，我会有一种瞬间的意识体验，能看到苹果的颜色和形状。

sentences.en: And I see it and then it fades and it comes back.
sentences.zh: 我看到了它，然后它消失了，又再次出现。

sentences.en: So people who don't have any mental imagery won't have that.
sentences.zh: 所以那些没有任何心理意象的人就不会有这种体验。

sentences.en: They will have a black on black experience.
sentences.zh: 他们会有一种黑上加黑的体验。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of different descriptions.
sentences.zh: 有各种各样的描述。

sentences.en: We hear about it like a black velvet with a black background.
sentences.zh: 我们听说过像黑色背景上的黑色天鹅绒那样的描述。

sentences.en: So there's almost something there, but not quite.
sentences.zh: 所以几乎有什么东西在那里，但又不太确定。

sentences.en: So that's sort of typically refers to the voluntary.
sentences.zh: 这通常指的是自主的（想象）。

sentences.en: I should also mention the voluntary creation of the mental image.
sentences.zh: 我还应该提到自主创造心理意象这一点。

sentences.en: So we can also dive into voluntary involuntary.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以深入探讨自主和非自主（想象）。

sentences.en: And interestingly, we've known about sort of the existence of aphantasia for quite a long time.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我们知道心盲症的存在已经有很长一段时间了。

sentences.en: So
sentences.zh: 所以

sentences.en: Francis Galton published his paper in about 1883, which has become very famous since then, where he had
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯·高尔顿在1883年左右发表了他的论文，此后变得非常出名，他在文中让

sentences.en: his friends and colleagues come in and sort of describe what they had for breakfast, what was on the breakfast table.
sentences.zh: 他的朋友和同事进来，描述他们早餐吃了什么，早餐桌上有什么。

sentences.en: And he discovered that some people could not recall or not recreate that mental image.
sentences.zh: 他发现有些人无法回忆起或无法重现那种心理意象。

sentences.en: And so he concluded that some part of the population has no ability to visualize.
sentences.zh: 因此他得出结论，部分人群没有视觉化想象的能力。

sentences.en: Then sort of over the, you know, many, many decades since then, you know, there's a few papers which
sentences.zh: 然后在那之后的几十年里，你知道，有几篇论文

sentences.en: touched on this idea of having no mental imagery, but it really wasn't till 2015 where a paper gave it the name, aphantasia coined this new name for it.
sentences.zh: 触及了这种没有心理意象的想法，但直到2015年才有一篇论文给它命名，创造了“心盲症”这个新名词。

sentences.en: And then there was a few media articles about it.
sentences.zh: 然后有一些关于它的媒体文章。

sentences.en: And then the idea kind of just took off in the sort of people's minds.
sentences.zh: 接着这个概念就在人们的脑海中流行起来了。

sentences.en: And I almost said imagination.
sentences.zh: 我刚才差点说成想象力了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's sort of just people started identifying with it and thinking about it and it's just, it's spread.
sentences.zh: 人们开始认同它，思考它，它就这样传播开了。

sentences.en: And so everywhere I go now and speak, you know, people know about it or people are discovering about it.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我走到哪里演讲，人们都知道它，或者正在发现它。

sentences.en: People are really fascinated about these individual differences in the way, the format of
sentences.zh: 人们对这种个体差异非常着迷，比如我们思维的格式，

sentences.en: our thoughts, things like this, how, you know, some people can think in pictures, other people can't.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情，你知道，有些人可以用图片思考，而有些人则不能。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 这意味着什么？

sentences.en: How are their brains different?
sentences.zh: 他们的大脑有何不同？

sentences.en: What does it mean to their everyday life, their creativity, their relationships, their jobs?
sentences.zh: 这对他们的日常生活、创造力、人际关系、工作意味着什么？

sentences.en: All these questions have been popping up.
sentences.zh: 所有这些问题都不断涌现。

sentences.en: So it's, you know, in the last sort of decade or so, the topic has just gotten so much attention and so much, yeah, scientific and general public attention.
sentences.zh: 所以，在过去十年左右的时间里，这个话题受到了极大的关注，受到了科学界和公众的广泛关注。

sentences.en: Well, let me ask you how common is aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 那么，请问心盲症有多普遍？

sentences.en: I mean, for those of us who don't have it, it's very hard to imagine not having a mental image.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对于我们这些没有心盲症的人来说，很难想象没有心理意象是什么样子。

sentences.en: I mean, you try to stop yourself.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你试着阻止自己。

sentences.en: If I say, don't think about an elephant, you're going to think about an elephant and you'll see it.
sentences.zh: 如果我说，不要去想大象，你还是会去想大象，并且会看到它。

sentences.en: One thing I'll say up front is that the main way to measure mental imagery or aphantasia at scale is using a questionnaire.
sentences.zh: 首先我要说的是，大规模测量心理意象或心盲症的主要方法是使用问卷调查。

sentences.en: And that's called the vividness of visual imagery questionnaire.
sentences.zh: 这被称为“视觉意象生动度问卷”。

sentences.en: And using that technique, we think the S sort of four or 5% of the population.
sentences.zh: 使用这种技术，我们认为大约有4%或5%的人口（患有此症）。

sentences.en: One of the downsides, I'm a huge fan of questionnaires, but one of the downsides is that a questionnaire like this is really examining two things at once.
sentences.zh: 缺点之一是——我非常喜欢问卷调查，但它的缺点之一是这种问卷实际上是在同时考察两件事。

sentences.en: It's examining someone's actual visual mental imagery, but it's also examining how they decide or their criteria for giving a number to that mental imagery.
sentences.zh: 它既在考察一个人的实际视觉心理意象，也在考察他们如何决定或他们为该心理意象打分的标准。

sentences.en: So you and me, Kim, could have the exact same mental imagery of a sunset and you could decide to give it a 2 and I could decide to give it a 4 or 5.
sentences.zh: 所以你和我，金，可能对日落有完全相同的心理意象，但你可能决定给它打2分，而我可能决定给它打4分或5分。

sentences.en: And that's our internal criteria or metacognition of our assessment of that.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们对评估结果的内在标准或元认知。

sentences.en: What we're also finding is that some people who have aphantasia have lived their lives thinking that the idea of mental imagery and visualization was a metaphor.
sentences.zh: 我们还发现，一些患有心盲症的人一生都认为心理意象和视觉化想象的概念只是一个比喻。

sentences.en: And so they assume that everyone had the same experience.
sentences.zh: 所以他们假设每个人都有相同的体验。

sentences.en: And so when they fill out a questionnaire, they tend to score it quite highly because they don't realize what mental imagery can be in others.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他们填写问卷时，他们往往会给出很高的分数，因为他们没有意识到心理意象在别人身上是什么样的。

sentences.en: And so we found quite a few of these people that when you then just talk about or
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现了相当多这样的人，当你和他们谈论，或者

sentences.en: give them a little video about what imagery can be, that it can be this conscious visual experience,
sentences.zh: 给他们看一段关于意象是什么的小视频，告诉他们这可以是一种有意识的视觉体验时，

sentences.en: they're genuinely shocked and they all often readjust their numbers in the questionnaire.
sentences.zh: 他们会感到非常震惊，并且经常会重新调整他们在问卷中的评分。

sentences.en: They're reported downwards.
sentences.zh: 他们的报告分数会下降。

sentences.en: So for those reasons, I suspect that, you know, the estimate might be a bit higher than the 5%, maybe in the 6%, 7%, 8% range.
sentences.zh: 所以出于这些原因，我怀疑这个估计值可能比5%要高一些，可能在6%、7%、8%左右。

sentences.en: But we haven't been able to use our more objective lab-based techniques to assess visual imagery on a large-scale study yet.
sentences.zh: 但我们还无法使用更客观的实验室技术在大规模研究中评估视觉意象。

sentences.en: Now, you've come up with a different technique, right?
sentences.zh: 那么，您已经提出了一种不同的技术，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's not just self-reports on a questionnaire.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不仅仅是问卷上的自我报告。

sentences.en: You have another method of measuring aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 您还有另一种测量心盲症的方法。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 能谈谈那个吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we've actually developed three different methods over the years.
sentences.zh: 是的，多年来我们实际上开发了三种不同的方法。

sentences.en: And the first one that sort of, you know, that was pivotal in my personal journey getting to study mental imagery
sentences.zh: 第一种方法，在我的个人研究心理意象的历程中起到了关键作用，

sentences.en: was using a visual illusion called binocular rivalry, which as it sounds is a rivalry between the images going into each eye.
sentences.zh: 是使用一种叫做“双眼竞争”的视觉错觉，顾名思义，就是进入每只眼睛的图像之间的竞争。

sentences.en: So if I put up a hand in front of one eye, my brain, my one eye, my right eye will see my hand, the other eye will see you on the computer screen.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我把一只手放在一只眼睛前，我的大脑，我的一只眼睛，我的右眼会看到我的手，另一只眼睛会看到电脑屏幕上的你。

sentences.en: And that puts my visual system into this state of conflict, hence rivalry.
sentences.zh: 这使我的视觉系统处于这种冲突状态，因此称为竞争。

sentences.en: And when you sort of balance those images out, you get these beautiful vacillations and oscillations of consciousness between whatever's going to one eye versus the other.
sentences.zh: 当你平衡这些图像时，你会得到这些美丽的意识波动和振荡，在进入一只眼睛的图像和另一只眼睛的图像之间切换。

sentences.en: And so we use that visual illusion, block to rivalry, to study consciousness in its own right.
sentences.zh: 所以我们利用这种视觉错觉——双眼竞争，来研究意识本身。

sentences.en: But I discovered many years ago that you could actually use the illusion as a way to measure mental imagery.
sentences.zh: 但我多年前发现，你实际上可以利用这种错觉作为测量心理意象的方法。

sentences.en: So how it works is, let's say we have a binocular rivalry stimulus set up.
sentences.zh: 它是这样工作的：假设我们设置了一个双眼竞争刺激。

sentences.en: So we have a red pattern and a green pattern, one going to each eye.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个红色图案和一个绿色图案，分别进入每只眼睛。

sentences.en: We just get participants to try and imagine one of those patterns.
sentences.zh: 我们只是让参与者尝试想象其中一个图案。

sentences.en: So they imagine, say the red pattern, then we just briefly flash on this binocular rivalry illusion.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想象，比如红色图案，然后我们短暂地闪现这个双眼竞争错觉。

sentences.en: And we found that what they imagine tended to be what they see.
sentences.zh: 我们发现他们想象的内容往往就是他们所看到的。

sentences.en: In other words, the content of their mental imagery, their visual imagery was biasing the way they saw this visual illusion.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们心理意象的内容，他们的视觉意象，正在偏向他们看待这种视觉错觉的方式。

sentences.en: You imagine red, you see red.
sentences.zh: 你想象红色，你就会看到红色。

sentences.en: You imagine green, you see green.
sentences.zh: 你想象绿色，你就会看到绿色。

sentences.en: And over a number of trials, that turned out to be a nice way to measure the sort of sensory strength of visual imagery.
sentences.zh: 经过多次试验，这被证明是测量视觉意象感官强度的一种很好的方法。

sentences.en: So that was the first method.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一种方法。

sentences.en: We've sort of developed two other methods.
sentences.zh: 我们还开发了另外两种方法。

sentences.en: Another way to do it is using emotional mental imagery.
sentences.zh: 另一种方法是使用情感心理意象。

sentences.en: So we have people come into the lab and they wear a little thing on their finger, which measures skin conductance.
sentences.zh: 我们让人进入实验室，在他们的手指上戴一个小东西，用来测量皮肤电导。

sentences.en: So just sort of the levels of micro sweat on the skin.
sentences.zh: 也就是皮肤上微汗的水平。

sentences.en: And then we have them read out these kind of scary scenarios.
sentences.zh: 然后让他们读出这些可怕的情景。

sentences.en: They're swimming in the ocean and a dark shadow moves underneath them.
sentences.zh: 他们在海里游泳，一个黑影在他们下方移动。

sentences.en: Something bumps their foot.
sentences.zh: 有什么东西撞到了他们的脚。

sentences.en: They look back at the beach and people are screaming, you know, and the shark gets closer and closer or they're rock climbing and their fingers start slipping.
sentences.zh: 他们回头看海滩，人们在尖叫，你知道，鲨鱼越来越近，或者他们在攀岩，手指开始打滑。

sentences.en: And we find that this skin conductance response, which is kind of a way to measure stress or anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我们发现这种皮肤电导反应，这是一种测量压力或焦虑的方法。

sentences.en: If you have mental imagery goes up as they're reading these stories.
sentences.zh: 如果你有心理意象，当你读这些故事时，它就会上升。

sentences.en: If people are doing the experiment who have a fantasia, you see more or less a noisy flat line.
sentences.zh: 如果做实验的人患有心盲症，你会看到一条嘈杂的平线。

sentences.en: So there's a difference in that sort of emotional or stress response.
sentences.zh: 所以这种情感或压力反应存在差异。

sentences.en: If you show both those groups, just, you know, scary images, pictures on the screen, you see the more or less the same response.
sentences.zh: 如果你给这两组人看同样的恐怖图像，屏幕上的图片，你会看到大致相同的反应。

sentences.en: So it does seem to be just the role of imagery in translating the words into ideas, into a visual imagery that drives more emotion.
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎只是意象在将文字转化为思想、转化为视觉意象从而驱动更多情感方面的作用。

sentences.en: And we'll see a bit later that this emotional response is one of the sort of big thematic differences between thinking in pictures or not thinking in pictures.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会看到，这种情感反应是“用图片思考”与“不用图片思考”之间最大的主题差异之一。

sentences.en: And just very quickly, the third way is using your pupil.
sentences.zh: 很快地说一下，第三种方法是使用你的瞳孔。

sentences.en: So people will know that if you look at a bright light, if you look at the sun, which you shouldn't, your pupil will constrict, right?
sentences.zh: 人们都知道，如果你看强光，如果你看太阳——你不应该这样做——你的瞳孔会收缩，对吧？

sentences.en: To protect your, to protect your, the neurons in your eye, let less light in.
sentences.zh: 为了保护你的眼睛里的神经元，让更少的光进入。

sentences.en: It turns out that if you imagine bright things or dark things, your pupil also responds.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，如果你想象明亮的事物或黑暗的事物，你的瞳孔也会做出反应。

sentences.en: So you get people into a dark room and you say, imagine you can just use simple shapes or you can use, you know, real objects.
sentences.zh: 所以你让人进入一个黑暗的房间，你说，想象——你可以只用简单的形状，或者你可以用真实的物体。

sentences.en: Imagine this under bright lights, a bright square or a dark square.
sentences.zh: 想象在强光下的明亮方块或黑暗方块。

sentences.en: And you'll see that people will also constrict when they're imagining the bright square.
sentences.zh: 你会看到人们在想象明亮方块时，瞳孔也会收缩。

sentences.en: So you can measure this with a little infrared camera quite easily.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以用一个小红外摄像机很容易地测量到这一点。

sentences.en: And it turns out that's also a nice way to measure mental imagery.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这也是测量心理意象的一种好方法。

sentences.en: If you don't have mental imagery and you try and do that task, your pupil doesn't respond.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有心理意象，而你尝试做那个任务，你的瞳孔就不会有反应。

sentences.en: Interestingly though, there's a nice control in that experiment that you can
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，那个实验中有一个很好的对照，你可以

sentences.en: get people to try and imagine one object, two objects, three objects, or four objects.
sentences.zh: 让人尝试想象一个物体、两个物体、三个物体或四个物体。

sentences.en: And the sort of mental load is more with more objects.
sentences.zh: 心理负荷随着物体数量的增加而增加。

sentences.en: And we see that the pupil also responds to this mental load.
sentences.zh: 我们看到瞳孔也会对这种心理负荷做出反应。

sentences.en: And we see that response in both groups, that those with visual imagery and those with aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 我们在两组人中都看到了这种反应，即那些有视觉意象的人和那些患有心盲症的人。

sentences.en: So that's a nice way to control because many people would say, oh, how do you know that people with aphantasia just aren't trying?
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个很好的对照方法，因为许多人会说，哦，你怎么知道患有心盲症的人不是没有尝试呢？

sentences.en: And so this sort of set size effect of the number of objects is a nice way to provide evidence that yes, people with aphantasia are indeed trying.
sentences.zh: 所以这种物体数量的集合大小效应是提供证据的好方法，证明患有心盲症的人确实在尝试。

sentences.en: We can see this difference.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到这种差异。

sentences.en: So that's really the three ways of measuring imagery.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是测量意象的三种方法。

sentences.en: Of course, you can use brain scanning, fMRI to look at the visual response in visual areas, but that's much slower and much more expensive.
sentences.zh: 当然，你可以使用脑扫描，即功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）来观察视觉区域的视觉反应，但这要慢得多，也昂贵得多。

sentences.en: But speaking of brains and fMRIs, what do we know about what's happening in the brains of people who have aphantasia?
sentences.zh: 说到大脑和fMRI，我们对心盲症患者大脑中发生的事情了解多少？

sentences.en: Do we have information from these brain studies?
sentences.zh: 我们有来自这些大脑研究的信息吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we have.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们有。

sentences.en: We've done brain stimulation studies and functional magnetic resonance imaging studies.
sentences.zh: 我们已经进行了大脑刺激研究和功能性磁共振成像研究。

sentences.en: We've done anatomical studies as well.
sentences.zh: 我们也进行了解剖学研究。

sentences.en: So first up, we have evidence that the size of visual cortex.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们有证据表明视觉皮层的大小。

sentences.en: So if everyone remembers the cerebral cortex around the outside is big sheet, but it's all sort of scrunched up to fit inside the skull.
sentences.zh: 如果每个人都记得大脑皮层外围是一张大薄片，但它为了塞进头骨里被挤压在一起。

sentences.en: Now you can measure that in a brain scanner, and then you can kind of flatten it out and measure the size of different brain areas.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以在脑扫描仪中测量它，然后你可以把它展平并测量不同大脑区域的大小。

sentences.en: And we've done that with visual cortex, the part of the back of the brain.
sentences.zh: 我们对视觉皮层，即大脑后部的部分做了这项工作。

sentences.en: And we find that those with a smaller visual cortex tend to have stronger mental imagery, which is interesting in itself.
sentences.zh: 我们发现那些视觉皮层较小的人往往有更强的心理意象，这本身就很有趣。

sentences.en: And there's also evidence that there are genes which contribute to the size of visual cortex.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有证据表明，某些基因与视觉皮层的大小有关。

sentences.en: So there's also emerging evidence that there might be some genetic components to aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 因此，目前也有越来越多的证据表明，失明症（aphantasia）可能存在一些遗传因素。

sentences.en: We've also done research looking at the cortical excitability of visual cortex.
sentences.zh: 我们还进行了研究，观察视觉皮层的皮层兴奋性。

sentences.en: So a nice way to think about that is there's all the neurons in your visual cortex.
sentences.zh: 思考这个问题的一个好方法是，想象你视觉皮层中的所有神经元。

sentences.en: Neurons are never just quiet and doing nothing.
sentences.zh: 神经元绝不会处于静止或无所事事的状态。

sentences.en: They're always sort of what seems like random firing.
sentences.zh: 它们似乎总是在进行某种随机的放电。

sentences.en: There's this baseline activity.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的基线活动。

sentences.en: We find that that baseline activity is also related to visual imagery strength.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，这种基线活动也与视觉意象的强度有关。

sentences.en: So the noisier those visual neurons are, the weaker the imagery tends to be, and the quieter they are, the stronger and clearer mental imagery seems to be.
sentences.zh: 视觉神经元越活跃（噪音越大），意象往往就越弱；而它们越安静，心理意象似乎就越强、越清晰。

sentences.en: Now we can measure that with TMS, transcranial magnetic stimulation, but we've also done a sort of
sentences.zh: 现在我们可以通过经颅磁刺激（TMS）来测量这一点，但我们也进行了一种

sentences.en: causative manipulation of that by using, um, a type of brain stimulation, which runs off a small battery, uh, TDCS or transcranial direct current stimulation.
sentences.zh: 因果操纵，即利用一种由小电池驱动的脑刺激技术，即经颅直流电刺激（TDCS）。

sentences.en: And when we do that, we can up or down regulate that sort of resting state cortical excitability.
sentences.zh: 当我们这样做时，我们可以上调或下调这种静息状态下的皮层兴奋性。

sentences.en: And we see that when we do that, that imagery can be, we can make it stronger or weaker.
sentences.zh: 我们观察到，当我们这样做时，意象确实可以变得更强或更弱。

sentences.en: These are not massive effects.
sentences.zh: 这些影响并不巨大。

sentences.en: They're quite small effects, but they are reliable.
sentences.zh: 它们的影响相当小，但却是可靠的。

sentences.en: And we're measuring these effects using that binocular ivory method I mentioned earlier.
sentences.zh: 我们正使用我之前提到的双眼竞争法来测量这些影响。

sentences.en: Then more recently, there's been a bunch of research we've done
sentences.zh: 最近，我们还进行了一系列研究，

sentences.en: looking at trying to decode mental images in visual cortex.
sentences.zh: 试图解码视觉皮层中的心理意象。

sentences.en: So we've known for a while that if you have mental imagery, when you imagine something, just like when you look at something, you can decode that
sentences.zh: 我们早就知道，如果你有心理意象，当你想象某样东西时，就像你看到某样东西时一样，你可以解码那种

sentences.en: pattern of activity and know what someone's looking at using sort of more modern fMRI techniques, algorithms, and a bit of AI sometimes.
sentences.zh: 活动模式，并利用更现代的fMRI技术、算法，有时甚至结合一点人工智能，来了解某人正在看什么。

sentences.en: Now it turns out, interestingly, you can also do that in people with aphantasia, which is kind of strange because they're saying they don't have any imagery.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，事实证明，患有失明症的人也可以做到这一点，这有点奇怪，因为他们声称自己没有任何意象。

sentences.en: They're trying, there's no conscious experience of imagery, but it seems like there's a decodable pattern in their visual cortex.
sentences.zh: 他们尝试了，虽然没有意识上的意象体验，但他们的视觉皮层中似乎存在一种可解码的模式。

sentences.en: So then the question then becomes, what is that pattern?
sentences.zh: 那么问题就变成了，那种模式是什么？

sentences.en: Why is it not conscious?
sentences.zh: 为什么它没有进入意识？

sentences.en: And that has started sort of these debates around this idea of unconscious imagery,
sentences.zh: 这引发了关于“无意识意象”这一概念的辩论，

sentences.en: and maybe there could be two different types of visual aphantasia, some sort of what people might
sentences.zh: 也许视觉失明症可以分为两种不同的类型，一种是人们可能

sentences.en: call like a true aphantasia with zero imagery, and another type where there is sort of some residual
sentences.zh: 称之为“完全失明症”，即零意象；另一种则是存在某种残留的

sentences.en: representation, and for unknown reasons at this stage, that representation remains unconscious,
sentences.zh: 表征，但由于目前未知的原因，这种表征保持在无意识状态，

sentences.en: maybe people can't pay attention to it, or for some other reason, the format is slightly different, and it just remains unconscious.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为人们无法关注它，或者由于其他原因，其格式略有不同，导致它一直处于无意识状态。

sentences.en: So that's where things are at the moment, and people are sort of getting excited about how to then sort of probe this idea further of unconscious imagery.
sentences.zh: 这就是目前的情况，人们开始对如何进一步探索这种“无意识意象”的想法感到兴奋。

sentences.en: There does seem to be other evidence we've collected from non-aphantasia research that if you do have
sentences.zh: 从非失明症的研究中，我们似乎收集到了其他证据，表明如果你确实拥有

sentences.en: visual imagery, you can have unconscious imagery, just like you can have unconscious visual perception,
sentences.zh: 视觉意象，你也可能拥有无意识意象，就像你可能拥有无意识的视觉感知一样，

sentences.en: kind of a tangent, but it does seem to be there.
sentences.zh: 这有点离题了，但它似乎确实存在。

sentences.en: So it could be that there is something similar happening with aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 所以失明症中可能也发生了类似的事情。

sentences.en: Do people with aphantasia dream?
sentences.zh: 失明症患者会做梦吗？

sentences.en: It turns out, yeah.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，会的。

sentences.en: All we have at this stage is questionnaire data.
sentences.zh: 目前我们掌握的只有问卷数据。

sentences.en: We haven't done the study that we'd love to do, which is a proper sleep study where we get people in the lab, and they have a sleep lab,
sentences.zh: 我们还没有进行我们非常想做的研究，即那种正规的睡眠研究，把人们带到实验室，让他们在睡眠实验室里，

sentences.en: but they sleep all night, and we wake them up and monitor their brain activity.
sentences.zh: 睡上一整晚，然后我们唤醒他们并监测他们的大脑活动。

sentences.en: But looking at the questionnaire data, it seems that some do, some don't.
sentences.zh: 但观察问卷数据，似乎有些人会做梦，有些人不会。

sentences.en: So when you average all the data, you do see significant differences in the amount of dreaming, the sensory qualities of the dream.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你对所有数据进行平均时，你会看到梦的数量和梦的感官质量存在显著差异。

sentences.en: But to really understand the data, you're going to kind of dig more on an individual level,
sentences.zh: 但要真正理解这些数据，你需要深入到个人层面去挖掘，

sentences.en: where some people report they have no memory of dreaMs. Some people report still dreams with emotional content, but less visual.
sentences.zh: 有些人报告说他们完全不记得梦，有些人报告说梦里仍有情感内容，但视觉感较少。

sentences.en: Some people report sort of black and white dreaMs. And so there's kind of a mixture state there, but there are certainly people that have aphantasia and do report dreaming.
sentences.zh: 有些人报告说梦是黑白的。所以情况比较复杂，但肯定有失明症患者报告说他们会做梦。

sentences.en: What about reading?
sentences.zh: 那阅读呢？

sentences.en: I mean, if you're going to read fiction, you are going to have a mental image of what's going on in the story.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你要读小说，你脑海中肯定会对故事的情节产生心理意象。

sentences.en: I mean, do people with aphantasia find reading fiction in particular so boring that they just can't do it?
sentences.zh: 那么，失明症患者是否觉得读小说特别无聊，以至于根本读不下去？

sentences.en: Well, not so boring that I never read a book, but there is emerging evidence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还没无聊到我从不看书的地步，但确实有新的证据出现。

sentences.en: And I think some papers are about to come out on this where, yeah, if you think about that study I mentioned before, where you're reading emotional
sentences.zh: 我想有些论文即将发表，内容是，是的，如果你想想我之前提到的那个研究，当你阅读情感

sentences.en: content, the skin conductance response was different.
sentences.zh: 内容时，皮肤电反应是不同的。

sentences.en: So you can think about that to reading an exciting or scary novel.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以联想到阅读一本激动人心或恐怖的小说。

sentences.en: Without those pictures in your mind, the experience is going to be, I don't like to use the word lacking, but at least in terms of emotional content, it probably will be lacking.
sentences.zh: 如果没有脑海中的那些画面，这种体验将会——我不喜欢用“缺失”这个词，但至少在情感内容方面，它可能会有所欠缺。

sentences.en: I don't want to make claims in other areas.
sentences.zh: 我不想在其他领域妄下结论。

sentences.en: And so because of that, yeah, there is some evidence now that people with aphantasia enjoy reading a little bit less when it comes to fiction or get a
sentences.zh: 正因如此，是的，现在有一些证据表明，失明症患者在阅读小说时享受程度稍低，或者

sentences.en: little bit less drawn into the stories.
sentences.zh: 不太容易被故事吸引。

sentences.en: And that's sort of that theme I mentioned earlier, that this idea of imagery as this virtual reality simulator that can amplify emotions.
sentences.zh: 这与我之前提到的主题有关，即意象作为一种可以放大情感的虚拟现实模拟器。

sentences.en: And so there's sort of this interesting link between thoughts and the emotional responses, the emotional parts of our brain, and imagery seems to sit there in the middle.
sentences.zh: 因此，思想与情感反应、大脑的情感部分之间存在着有趣的联系，而意象似乎就处于中间位置。

sentences.en: And it's almost like if you have imagery, it can kind of trick the emotional parts in your brain to thinking the content of imagery is actually happening.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像是如果你有意象，它就能欺骗大脑的情感部分，让它认为意象的内容正在真实发生。

sentences.en: And so it responds more.
sentences.zh: 因此，它会做出更强烈的反应。

sentences.en: So I mentioned that skin conductance response, we have done studies looking at risk perception, looking at empathy, looking at mind wandering,
sentences.zh: 所以我提到了皮肤电反应，我们还做过研究，观察风险感知、同理心、思维游离，

sentences.en: and we've done studies looking at models of PTSD.
sentences.zh: 我们还做过关于创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）模型的研究。

sentences.en: So PTSD, lab-based models of PTSD where people come into the lab and watch a real sort of pretty unpleasant video.
sentences.zh: 也就是PTSD的实验室模型，人们来到实验室观看一段相当令人不快的真实视频。

sentences.en: And then we send them home with an app that sort of they monitor every time they think about that video or have an image pop
sentences.zh: 然后我们让他们带着一个应用程序回家，每当他们想到那个视频，或者脑海中突然浮现出图像，

sentences.en: into their head or have any thoughts pop into their head.
sentences.zh: 或者脑海中浮现出任何想法时，他们都会进行记录。

sentences.en: And we see stark differences there between those that have imagery and aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 我们看到有无意象和失明症的人之间存在显著差异。

sentences.en: And when they do think about that video, the emotional response and how disruptive it is to their life is very different.
sentences.zh: 当他们想到那个视频时，情感反应以及它对生活的干扰程度是非常不同的。

sentences.en: So across all those examples, sort of the empathy, the mind wandering, some moral dilemma stuff we're doing now,
sentences.zh: 所以，在所有这些例子中，无论是同理心、思维游离，还是我们现在正在做的道德困境研究，

sentences.en: it seems that this emotional response to thoughts, thought simulations is just different with or without imagery.
sentences.zh: 似乎这种对思想和思维模拟的情感反应，在有无意象的情况下就是不同。

sentences.en: So sort of from anxiety through to basically anything that you think would benefit or be different with a sort of virtual simulation of the thing, a sensory simulation
sentences.zh: 所以，从焦虑到基本上任何你认为会受益于某种虚拟模拟、感官模拟的事情，

sentences.en: does seem to be different.
sentences.zh: 似乎确实有所不同。

sentences.en: And that would include, you know, addiction and cravings, you know, a lot of things there.
sentences.zh: 这包括成瘾和渴望，你知道，很多事情都包含在内。

sentences.en: So that is probably the biggest difference we see in thinking with images or thinking without images.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是我们看到的有无意象思维之间最大的区别。

sentences.en: I am wondering if there's a relationship between aphantasia and prosopagnosia or face blindness.
sentences.zh: 我想知道失明症和脸盲症（prosopagnosia）之间是否有联系。

sentences.en: If you don't have a mental image of the things you have experienced, does that affect whether you can recognize people or places you've seen before?
sentences.zh: 如果你对自己经历过的事情没有心理意象，这会影响你识别以前见过的人或地方的能力吗？

sentences.en: There are studies, we've done studies on episodic memory, so lifelong memories.
sentences.zh: 有一些研究，我们对情景记忆，也就是终身记忆进行了研究。

sentences.en: And we find that using this sort of interview style techniques, we've got to remember events that happened,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，使用这种访谈式的技巧，我们让人们回忆过去发生的事情，

sentences.en: you know, a month ago, six months ago, years, 10 years ago, that those with aphantasia recall less details about very similar events compared to those with imagery.
sentences.zh: 比如一个月前、六个月前、几年前、十年前发生的事，失明症患者对非常相似事件的回忆细节比有视觉意象的人要少。

sentences.en: Of course, the vividness, the emotionality of those experiences are also different, but the details thing is kind of quite interesting.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些经历的生动性和情感色彩也不同，但细节方面的问题确实相当有趣。

sentences.en: And it's not devastatingly different.
sentences.zh: 而且这种差异并不是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: It's not like there's no details, there's still plenty of details, but it is significantly different or significantly more details if you have imagery.
sentences.zh: 并不是说完全没有细节，仍然有很多细节，但如果有意象的话，细节确实显著不同或显著更多。

sentences.en: So the memory of experiences in our lives does seem to be different.
sentences.zh: 所以我们生活中经历的记忆似乎确实不同。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you have an image attached to that memory or can recreate that image, I think there's some evidence potentially linking prosopagnosia.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果你有一个与记忆相关的图像，或者能够重现那个图像，我认为有一些证据可能与脸盲症有关。

sentences.en: I don't know how strong that evidence is.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这些证据有多强。

sentences.en: I have certainly come across individuals, not many, just like two or three who claim to have
sentences.zh: 我确实遇到过一些人，不多，也就两三个人，他们声称拥有

sentences.en: a very specific version of aphantasia, which is face specific and human face specific.
sentences.zh: 一种非常特殊的失明症，即针对面孔的，特别是人类面孔的失明症。

sentences.en: So it's kind of like a prosopagnosia version of aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像是失明症的脸盲版本。

sentences.en: They say they can imagine, you know, their dog's face, fine, but they can't imagine human faces.
sentences.zh: 他们说他们可以想象他们狗的脸，没问题，但他们无法想象人脸。

sentences.en: They can still recognize them, but they just can't imagine them.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然可以认出人，只是无法在脑海中想象出来。

sentences.en: So it's not just prosopagnosia, it's like an imagery version of prosopagnosia.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是脸盲症，这更像是脸盲症的意象版本。

sentences.en: Again, only a handful of cases I've seen of that.
sentences.zh: 同样，我只见过少数几个这样的案例。

sentences.en: But yeah, there certainly does seem to be these differences with memory and the amount of information you can recall.
sentences.zh: 但确实，在记忆力和你能回忆起的信息量方面，似乎确实存在这些差异。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break.
sentences.zh: 我们要休息一下。

sentences.en: When we return, I'll talk with Dr. Pearson about what it's like to have
sentences.zh: 回来后，我将与皮尔逊博士（Dr. Pearson）讨论拥有

sentences.en: hyperphantasia or extremely vivid, detailed mental imagery.
sentences.zh: 超意象（hyperphantasia）或极其生动、详细的心理意象是什么样的体验。

sentences.en: Let's talk about the other side of the coin, which is the people who have constant images or a hyperphantasia where it's extremely vivid and detailed in their minds all the time.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈硬币的另一面，也就是那些拥有持续意象或超意象的人，他们的脑海中始终存在极其生动和详细的画面。

sentences.en: I mean, how common is that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种情况有多普遍？

sentences.en: And do we all just sort of fall somewhere in between one or the other?
sentences.zh: 我们是否都处于两者之间的某个位置？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there does seem to be almost a normal distribution or at least something that's shaped like that.
sentences.zh: 似乎确实存在一种正态分布，或者至少是某种形状类似的东西。

sentences.en: It's where there's this sort of bell curve where most people fall in the middle somewhere, and then you have these tails that get thin on the end.
sentences.zh: 就像钟形曲线一样，大多数人落在中间的某个位置，然后两端会变得稀疏。

sentences.en: There's been much less research done on what's called hyperphantasia, or if you go back a few decades, it was called idatic imagery.
sentences.zh: 关于所谓的“超意象”的研究要少得多，如果追溯到几十年前，它被称为“遗觉意象”（eidetic imagery）。

sentences.en: There was a whole field of research into what was called idatic imagery in children back sort of last century, looking at this idea that children
sentences.zh: 上个世纪，关于儿童“遗觉意象”的研究曾是一个完整的领域，研究的是11岁、10岁以下的儿童

sentences.en: under 11, under 10 years old had much stronger imagery than something would happen during their teenage years, and the imagery would get sort of get weaker.
sentences.zh: 拥有比青少年时期更强的意象，随着年龄增长，意象会变弱。

sentences.en: Again, some of that research is a bit dated now.
sentences.zh: 同样，其中一些研究现在已经有点过时了。

sentences.en: We don't have the same techniques for measuring these things that we, you know, they didn't
sentences.zh: 我们没有测量这些东西的相同技术，你知道，他们当时没有

sentences.en: have those techniques back then, so we don't know a lot about that using modern techniques.
sentences.zh: 那些技术，所以我们对使用现代技术的研究了解不多。

sentences.en: Because aphantasia gets a lot of media attention, we have huge databases with many thousands of people
sentences.zh: 因为失明症受到了很多媒体的关注，我们拥有庞大的数据库，包含成千上万名

sentences.en: that have aphantasia, but in comparison, we have a very small database for those that have
sentences.zh: 患有失明症的人，但相比之下，我们对于那些拥有

sentences.en: hyperphantasia.
sentences.zh: 超意象的人的数据库非常小。

sentences.en: And again, it's clearer and easier to define aphantasia as the complete absence, you know, you have imagery or you don't have imagery.
sentences.zh: 同样，将失明症定义为完全缺失更清晰、更容易，你知道，要么你有意象，要么你没有。

sentences.en: There's kind of a step function there, whereas it's harder to define the upper end of this hyperphantasia.
sentences.zh: 那里有一种阶梯函数，而定义超意象的上限则更难。

sentences.en: When does strong imagery become hyper or not?
sentences.zh: 强意象何时变成超意象？

sentences.en: And it can be a bit of an arbitrary cutoff.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个有点随意的界限。

sentences.en: And I think as we do more research into this, we will end up defining it more to do with things like false memories.
sentences.zh: 我认为随着我们对此进行更多研究，我们最终会将其定义为与虚假记忆等事物相关。

sentences.en: So I know some people with very strong imagery who will literally have confusions about whether they imagined a scenario or whether it actually happened.
sentences.zh: 我知道一些拥有非常强意象的人，他们确实会混淆自己是想象了一个场景，还是它真的发生了。

sentences.en: There's a reason that most of us will forget our dreams, so we don't have reality confusion with our dreaMs. But if you have very strong imagery, and then you remember that, not
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人会忘记梦境是有原因的，所以我们不会对梦境产生现实混淆。但如果你有非常强的意象，然后你记住了它，这不仅

sentences.en: only could it sort of affect your sort of eyewitness memory of an event, you can sort of, you imagine something and then that gets reconsolidated back into the original memory.
sentences.zh: 会影响你对事件的目击记忆，你还可以想象某件事，然后它被重新整合回原始记忆中。

sentences.en: You can also just have confusion between whether something actually happened at all and the visual image.
sentences.zh: 你还可能仅仅在某事是否真的发生过与视觉图像之间产生混淆。

sentences.en: So we've done research into individuals with Parkinson's disease who have visual hallucinations.
sentences.zh: 我们对患有视觉幻觉的帕金森病患者进行了研究。

sentences.en: And we find that those with visual hallucinations have very strong imagery as measured using the binocular ivory technique.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，使用双眼竞争技术测量，那些有视觉幻觉的人拥有非常强的意象。

sentences.en: We also see people who have schizophrenia have not only the auditory stuff, but they have very strong visual imagery.
sentences.zh: 我们也看到精神分裂症患者不仅有听觉方面的问题，而且有非常强的视觉意象。

sentences.en: And also we see this trend in schizotypy sort of individuals as well.
sentences.zh: 而且我们在精神分裂型人格（schizotypy）个体中也看到了这种趋势。

sentences.en: So on the spectrum towards schizophrenia, we see that this association between strong imagery and anxiety and
sentences.zh: 因此，在向精神分裂症发展的谱系上，我们看到了强意象与焦虑和

sentences.en: PTSD as well.
sentences.zh: PTSD之间的这种关联。

sentences.en: So there's this kind of theme emerging there that some psychological and neurological disorders are associated with stronger mental imagery.
sentences.zh: 所以出现了一个主题，即一些心理和神经系统疾病与更强的心理意象有关。

sentences.en: And so you could make the case that everything else being equal, you know, if you had to choose between very, very strong imagery and very, very weak or zero
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说，在其他条件相同的情况下，如果你必须在非常非常强的意象和非常非常弱或零

sentences.en: imagery, you may actually want to choose aphantasia just because of this association with, you know, psychological and neurological disorders.
sentences.zh: 意象之间做出选择，你可能实际上会选择失明症，仅仅是因为它与心理和神经系统疾病的这种关联。

sentences.en: But we know less about that, the high end hyperphantasia than the aphantasia at this stage.
sentences.zh: 但现阶段我们对高端的超意象了解不如对失明症了解得多。

sentences.en: So we don't know a lot, but I've certainly met individuals who say they can, they can sort of replay a whole film and they swear to me, their conscious experience is like
sentences.zh: 所以我们了解不多，但我确实遇到过一些人，他们说他们可以重播整部电影，他们向我发誓，他们的意识体验就像

sentences.en: watching it on an iPad.
sentences.zh: 在iPad上观看一样。

sentences.en: It's that clear.
sentences.zh: 就是那么清晰。

sentences.en: No, I absolutely can't do that.
sentences.zh: 不，我绝对做不到。

sentences.en: So it's, it is hard for me to believe that, but they, I've only met one or two people that say that, and we haven't had a
sentences.zh: 所以，这对我来说很难相信，但我只遇到过一两个这样的人，我们还没有

sentences.en: chance to study them in detail yet, but there are seemingly individuals who can do that.
sentences.zh: 机会详细研究他们，但确实似乎有人能做到这一点。

sentences.en: So yeah, that's a big difference from no imagery at all.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这与完全没有意象有很大区别。

sentences.en: Does aphantasia exist only for visual images?
sentences.zh: 失明症只存在于视觉意象中吗？

sentences.en: I guess my question is, is it possible to have the equivalent of aphantasia for other senses, say being unable to hear music in your mind or recall a smell or a texture?
sentences.zh: 我想问的是，是否可能在其他感官上也存在等同于失明症的情况，比如无法在脑海中听到音乐，或无法回忆起气味或质地？

sentences.en: Yeah, great question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 是的，好问题，Kim。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对可以。

sentences.en: So it does, it's not just visual, you can have full multi-sensory aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 所以它不仅仅是视觉上的，你可能会有完全的多感官失明症。

sentences.en: So we've done some, some research where we, you know, measured a few thousand people and ran a sort of clustering
sentences.zh: 我们做了一些研究，测量了几千人，并进行了一种聚类

sentences.en: analysis or a bunch of different clustering analysis to see the, the groupings.
sentences.zh: 分析或一系列不同的聚类分析来观察分组情况。

sentences.en: And we found that, yeah, most people who had aphantasia tended to have this full multi-sensory aphantasia, but there was also a significant group that just had pure visual.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，大多数患有失明症的人倾向于拥有这种完全的多感官失明症，但也有一个显著的群体只有纯粹的视觉失明症。

sentences.en: And then we found all the other groupings you could imagine, but in very small quantities or proportions.
sentences.zh: 然后我们发现了你能想象到的所有其他分组，但数量或比例非常小。

sentences.en: So you could have a pure auditory aphantasia, you could have auditory and visual, but they were very small groups compared
sentences.zh: 所以你可以有纯粹的听觉失明症，你可以有听觉和视觉的，但与

sentences.en: to the sort of larger groups of pure visual or pure multi-sensory across all the senses.
sentences.zh: 纯视觉或跨越所有感官的纯多感官的大群体相比，它们是非常小的群体。

sentences.en: And so there is a bias there in that the databases and the people we test have heard about aphantasia as a visual thing.
sentences.zh: 这里存在一种偏差，因为数据库和我们测试的人都听说过失明症是一种视觉现象。

sentences.en: So of course, there's going to be more people in the database that have visual aphantasia, but the clusterings do exist there.
sentences.zh: 所以当然，数据库中会有更多患有视觉失明症的人，但聚类确实存在。

sentences.en: And you can also drill down and there's people that have sort of auditory aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 你也可以深入挖掘，有些人患有某种听觉失明症。

sentences.en: And then there's also a subgroup which might be able to imagine music and sounds, but don't have an sort of inner mind's voice, if you like.
sentences.zh: 还有一个亚组，他们可能能够想象音乐和声音，但没有所谓的内心独白。

sentences.en: When they read, they don't hear the mental version of words being read to them.
sentences.zh: 当他们阅读时，听不到脑海中文字被朗读出来的声音。

sentences.en: They can't talk to themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们无法与自己对话。

sentences.en: And that's actually starting to grow into its own sort of subfield now of sort of the inner workings of the mind and the inner voice.
sentences.zh: 这实际上正开始发展成为一个独立的子领域，研究的是思维的内在运作和内心独白。

sentences.en: But absolutely, imagery can be across any of the senses, which is pretty interesting in itself.
sentences.zh: 但毋庸置疑，意象可以跨越任何感官，这本身就非常有趣。

sentences.en: And I often have thought about this, we've written about this a bit, that you don't really have a version of multi-sensory blindness, for example.
sentences.zh: 我经常思考这个问题，我们也写过一些相关文章，比如，你其实并没有一种“多感官失明”的情况。

sentences.en: I can't think of an individual in history that has had no sensory abilities across all their senses.
sentences.zh: 我想不出历史上有什么人是所有感官都完全丧失感知能力的。

sentences.en: No sight, no sound, no touch, no taste, no smell.
sentences.zh: 没有视觉、听觉、触觉、味觉和嗅觉。

sentences.en: I don't think we've ever had that.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们曾遇到过这种情况。

sentences.en: But the fact that you can have that in aphantasia already tells you something interesting about the differences between mental imagery across the
sentences.zh: 但你在“心盲症”（aphantasia）中能观察到这一点，这本身就揭示了跨感官心理意象与感官知觉之间的一些有趣差异，

sentences.en: senses and sensory perception, that there is something more central going on there, that you can have all these things not existing together.
sentences.zh: 说明大脑中存在某种更核心的机制，使得这些感官功能可以同时缺失。

sentences.en: Let me switch topics here a little bit.
sentences.zh: 让我稍微转换一下话题。

sentences.en: I know you've studied the connection between aphantasia and creativity.
sentences.zh: 我知道你研究过心盲症与创造力之间的联系。

sentences.en: What have you found?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: What is the relationship?
sentences.zh: 它们之间是什么关系？

sentences.en: Yeah, so we've done a bunch of research on this.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们在这方面做过很多研究。

sentences.en: We haven't yet published them.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有发表这些成果。

sentences.en: It's kind of a bit of a pipeline in the lab, sort of a clogged up pipeline of publications at the present.
sentences.zh: 目前实验室里积压了不少待发表的论文，就像一条堵塞的管道。

sentences.en: But in some, we found that there was no clear differences between those that have aphantasia
sentences.zh: 但在一些研究中，我们发现心盲症患者与拥有意象能力的人之间，

sentences.en: and those that have imagery in the sort of the classic ways of trying to measure creativity.
sentences.zh: 在衡量创造力的经典方式上并没有明显的差异。

sentences.en: And this is this divergent thinking, tasks like, you know, here's a brick.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的发散性思维，比如，给你一块砖头。

sentences.en: How many different ways could you use the brick?
sentences.zh: 你能想出多少种使用这块砖头的方法？

sentences.en: And then you have independent people score that on, you know, how creative it is and also how many different uses and things like that.
sentences.zh: 然后由独立的人员来评估其创造性，以及想出的用途数量等等。

sentences.en: So despite what people think and say that aphantasia is holding back their creativity at work or something, the data doesn't really support that because we
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管人们认为并声称心盲症会阻碍他们的工作创造力之类，但数据并不支持这种说法，因为我们

sentences.en: didn't see any differences.
sentences.zh: 没有看到任何差异。

sentences.en: And then having said that, you know, we've had aphantasia visual art exhibitions.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我们确实举办过心盲症患者的视觉艺术展。

sentences.en: Ed Catmull, who co-founded Pixar and ran that and then ran Disney Studios for many years, a good friend of mine, he has aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 皮克斯动画工作室的联合创始人艾德·卡特姆（Ed Catmull），他曾长期执掌皮克斯和迪士尼工作室，也是我的好朋友，他就是心盲症患者。

sentences.en: So he was crucial early on in coming up with some of the ideas and methods for doing computer design and using these sort of geometric shapes to define a square or a sphere.
sentences.zh: 他在早期构思计算机设计理念和方法时起到了关键作用，比如利用几何形状来定义正方形或球体。

sentences.en: And he said that if he could visualize the shapes, he probably wouldn't have come up with this mathematical geometry, these little triangles and things to describe these shapes.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果他能进行视觉化想象，可能反而想不出这种数学几何方法，即用这些小三角形等来描述形状。

sentences.en: And so he almost credits aphantasia and helping him with some of these breakthroughs in these sort of 3D designs.
sentences.zh: 所以他几乎将自己在3D设计领域的一些突破归功于心盲症。

sentences.en: Also one of their top animators, I'm blanking on the gentleman's name, but he was one of the top person who did a lot of the little mermaid designs for the characters.
sentences.zh: 还有他们的一位顶级动画师，我一时想不起他的名字了，但他曾负责《小美人鱼》中许多角色的设计。

sentences.en: He has aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 他也是心盲症患者。

sentences.en: And so I don't want anyone to think that, you know, if you have aphantasia, it's some barrier to being creative or starting an enterprise or a business or any of these things.
sentences.zh: 所以我不想让任何人认为，如果你有心盲症，它就是你发挥创造力、创业或做任何事情的障碍。

sentences.en: It does not seem to be the case.
sentences.zh: 事实似乎并非如此。

sentences.en: So I think it's important to get that out there.
sentences.zh: 我认为把这一点传达出去很重要。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I didn't want to give the impression either that aphantasia is some kind of a disorder that needs to be fixed.
sentences.zh: 我也不想给人留下一种印象，即心盲症是一种需要“治愈”的疾病。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems from what
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，根据我所读到的内容，

sentences.en: I've been reading anyway, and you would know better than I, that people who have it don't feel that they're in any way held back in life.
sentences.zh: 而且你比我更了解，那些患有此症的人并不觉得自己的生活受到了任何阻碍。

sentences.en: But I'm wondering if there are interventions.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇是否有什么干预手段。

sentences.en: So if somebody said, yeah, I'd like to know what it's like to have a visual internal life, is there anything that can be done to help with that?
sentences.zh: 如果有人说，是的，我想体验一下拥有视觉化的内心生活是什么感觉，有什么办法可以帮助他们吗？

sentences.en: Like I said, I mentioned earlier, we've done the study using that sort of that type of brain stimulation where we have up or down regulated imagery strength.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，我们做过一项研究，利用那种脑刺激技术来上调或下调意象强度。

sentences.en: All those participants had some form of imagery to begin with.
sentences.zh: 所有参与者最初都具备某种形式的意象能力。

sentences.en: Now, separately, we've done a five-day experiment where we had people come into the lab and practice their imagery every day for one hour for five days in a row.
sentences.zh: 另外，我们还做过一个为期五天的实验，让人们每天到实验室练习一小时意象，连续五天。

sentences.en: And while they were practicing, you know, we were measuring it using that binocular rivalry technique.
sentences.zh: 在他们练习时，我们使用双眼竞争技术进行测量。

sentences.en: And we didn't really see any improvement over that time.
sentences.zh: 在那段时间里，我们并没有看到明显的改善。

sentences.en: Now, that doesn't mean it's not trainable.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着它无法训练。

sentences.en: The thing with brain stimulation is it's not magically going to tell you how to create a mental image in the same way that if you wanted to learn a new language, let's
sentences.zh: 脑刺激的问题在于，它不会神奇地告诉你如何创造心理意象，就像如果你想学习一门新语言，

sentences.en: say you can't speak Chinese and you want to learn Chinese.
sentences.zh: 比如你不会说中文，你想学中文。

sentences.en: While I can stimulate the language areas of your brain, and that would improve your performance somewhat, it's not going to magically give
sentences.zh: 虽然我可以刺激你大脑中的语言区域，这会稍微提高你的表现，但它不会神奇地赋予

sentences.en: you the ability and the knowledge to speak Chinese.
sentences.zh: 你讲中文的能力和知识。

sentences.en: So I think the answer may be in combining practice with brain stimulation.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为答案可能在于将练习与脑刺激相结合。

sentences.en: Now, there is an emerging trend that has not, to my knowledge, been studied scientifically yet of this image streaming technique that came from photography, where people would
sentences.zh: 目前有一种新兴趋势，据我所知尚未经过科学研究，即源自摄影领域的“意象流”技术，人们首先

sentences.en: first have their eyes open and look at a room and then verbally out loud describe the visual details as much as possible.
sentences.zh: 睁开眼睛观察一个房间，然后尽可能大声地口头描述视觉细节。

sentences.en: And they do this over and over.
sentences.zh: 他们反复进行这个过程。

sentences.en: And this came from photography, where they was trying to, you know, design and the right way to set up a photograph.
sentences.zh: 这源于摄影，当时人们试图设计出设置照片的最佳方式。

sentences.en: And then the idea is then you close your eyes and try and do it by memory.
sentences.zh: 然后，接下来的想法是闭上眼睛，尝试凭记忆重现。

sentences.en: And it's important, apparently, that you do this out loud.
sentences.zh: 显然，大声说出来这一点很重要。

sentences.en: So there's a few groups online, in particular on YouTube now, who are talking about that as a way
sentences.zh: 所以现在网上有一些群体，特别是在YouTube上，正在讨论将其作为一种

sentences.en: to train mental imagery or give people mental imagery experience.
sentences.zh: 训练心理意象或赋予人们心理意象体验的方法。

sentences.en: Now, I know some people who have tried that and they haven't really noticed much difference.
sentences.zh: 我知道有些人尝试过，但并没有感觉到太大的区别。

sentences.en: Some people claim that they have.
sentences.zh: 有些人声称他们有效果。

sentences.en: And so again, it may be the case that some people who have aphantasia have some residual imagery, and that can be trained up.
sentences.zh: 所以同样，可能有些心盲症患者确实保留了一些残余的意象能力，可以通过训练增强。

sentences.en: And part of that equation might be simply teaching people what to pay attention to because they don't even know what imagery is in the first place.
sentences.zh: 其中的一部分可能仅仅是教人们如何去注意，因为他们甚至不知道什么是意象。

sentences.en: I should also mention there's two published case studies.
sentences.zh: 我还应该提到有两个已发表的案例研究。

sentences.en: They're retrospective studies from people who have done, been part of psychedelic research.
sentences.zh: 它们是对参与过迷幻药研究的人员进行的回顾性研究。

sentences.en: And at least two of those individuals, and by retrospective, they won't set out to beforehand to study mental imagery.
sentences.zh: 其中至少有两个人，之所以说是回顾性，是因为他们并非事先就打算研究心理意象。

sentences.en: They kind of discovered this along the way.
sentences.zh: 他们是在过程中偶然发现的。

sentences.en: And so it does rely on their memory of what the imagery was like before they took part in the psychedelic research.
sentences.zh: 因此，这依赖于他们对参与迷幻药研究前意象体验的记忆。

sentences.en: And they say that not only did they have the experience of imagery during the effect of the molecule, but that lasted afterwards as well.
sentences.zh: 他们说，不仅在药物作用期间有了意象体验，而且这种体验在事后也持续存在。

sentences.en: And that has given them imagery.
sentences.zh: 这赋予了他们意象能力。

sentences.en: Now, because it's just these two case studies, we have no idea whether these are two out of a thousand people, or would this work for everyone?
sentences.zh: 由于这只是两个案例研究，我们不知道这是否是千分之一的概率，还是对每个人都有效？

sentences.en: I certainly have talked to people who have taken part in psychedelic research and have aphantasia, and it didn't change their imagery.
sentences.zh: 我确实和一些参与过迷幻药研究的心盲症患者谈过，这并没有改变他们的意象能力。

sentences.en: So I don't think it's going to work for everyone.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为它不会对每个人都有效。

sentences.en: But there's some interesting things possibly emerging there, because we know that psychedelics will do a few things.
sentences.zh: 但其中可能出现了一些有趣的东西，因为我们知道迷幻药会产生一些作用。

sentences.en: But one of the things it does is put your brain to this very plastic state where it can rewire quite quickly.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是让大脑进入一种非常可塑的状态，可以很快地进行重连。

sentences.en: And so that's very interesting in respect to aphantasia and mental imagery.
sentences.zh: 所以这在心盲症和心理意象方面非常有趣。

sentences.en: So just to wrap up, what might studying aphantasia and hyperphantasia tell us more broadly about how the human mind works?
sentences.zh: 最后总结一下，研究心盲症和超意象症（hyperphantasia）能让我们更广泛地了解人类思维是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: I think first up, it's a really powerful and nice example of cognitive and neural diversity across the human experience.
sentences.zh: 我认为首先，它是人类体验中认知和神经多样性的一个非常有力且美妙的例证。

sentences.en: Another way to phrase all this would be that the format, right?
sentences.zh: 换一种说法就是，这种格式，对吧？

sentences.en: The format of your thoughts does change your life, and it changes the way you think.
sentences.zh: 你思维的格式确实会改变你的生活，并改变你的思考方式。

sentences.en: It changes how much you might donate to a charity.
sentences.zh: 它会改变你向慈善机构捐款的金额。

sentences.en: It changes your risk perception.
sentences.zh: 它会改变你对风险的感知。

sentences.en: So anytime your thoughts will take on the format of a depictive picture in your brain and mind, then that will nudge you and change the way you think,
sentences.zh: 所以，每当你的思维在大脑中以描绘性图像的格式呈现时，它就会推动并改变你的思考方式，

sentences.en: almost like a cognitive bias or a nudge in that language.
sentences.zh: 就像认知偏差或某种语言上的暗示一样。

sentences.en: So that in itself is really interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这本身就非常有趣。

sentences.en: I think also it teaches us about the internal types of consciousness research.
sentences.zh: 我认为它也让我们了解了内在意识研究的类型。

sentences.en: I've also always been fascinated by consciousness studies.
sentences.zh: 我一直对意识研究很着迷。

sentences.en: And I think imagery is one of the ways to study internal consciousness.
sentences.zh: 我认为意象是研究内在意识的途径之一。

sentences.en: In visual neuroscience, one of the things that's really hard to study is feedback signals.
sentences.zh: 在视觉神经科学中，很难研究的一件事就是反馈信号。

sentences.en: So we know that there's more signals that go backwards, if you like, in the brain than forwards.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，大脑中向后传递的信号比向前传递的要多。

sentences.en: So forwards means from my retina and my eye, back to visual cortex, and up to the higher levels of the brain.
sentences.zh: 向前意味着从视网膜和眼睛，传回视觉皮层，再传到大脑的高级区域。

sentences.en: But there's more connections that go backwards in many parts of the brain.
sentences.zh: 但在大脑的许多部位，向后的连接更多。

sentences.en: And we don't know a lot about what those do.
sentences.zh: 我们对这些连接的功能知之甚少。

sentences.en: And it's very hard to study.
sentences.zh: 而且研究起来非常困难。

sentences.en: But voluntary visual imagery is one of the few cases where you can have the eyes closed, have no visual stimulation, have someone imagine something,
sentences.zh: 但自主视觉意象是少数几种可以闭上眼睛、没有视觉刺激、让人想象某事，

sentences.en: and then study those feedback signals that are involved in visualizing mental imagery in a very pure isolated format.
sentences.zh: 然后以一种非常纯粹、孤立的格式研究参与视觉化心理意象的反馈信号的情况之一。

sentences.en: By that very definition, we stand to learn a lot about sensory perception from studying mental imagery.
sentences.zh: 根据这个定义，通过研究心理意象，我们有望对感官知觉有更多的了解。

sentences.en: And if I want to be controversial and probably annoy my colleagues in the vision science community, I would say the key to understanding vision would actually be,
sentences.zh: 如果我想引起争议并可能惹恼视觉科学界的同事，我会说理解视觉的关键实际上是，

sentences.en: one of the keys to understanding vision would be visual imagery.
sentences.zh: 理解视觉的关键之一就是视觉意象。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, the neurodiversity, the understanding of feedback, understanding consciousness, all those things, I think,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，神经多样性、对反馈的理解、对意识的理解，所有这些，我认为，

sentences.en: end up being really important contributions to science in general, to psychology and neuroscience.
sentences.zh: 最终都成为对科学、心理学和神经科学的重要贡献。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Pearson, I want to thank you for joining me.
sentences.zh: 好的，皮尔逊博士，感谢您接受我的采访。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这非常有意思。

sentences.en: I think you're working in a very unusual part of psychology.
sentences.zh: 我认为您正在心理学的一个非常独特的领域工作。

sentences.en: So thanks so much for sharing your knowledge.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您分享您的知识。

sentences.en: Oh, my pleasure, Kim.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是我的荣幸，金。

sentences.en: Great to talk today.
sentences.zh: 今天谈话很愉快。
